profile.reading:
SAP identifies this El Paso County, Colorado location, in the InterQuest Ridge area on the north side of Colorado Springs, under the internal facility code COS02. SAP SE is a German enterprise software company founded in 1972 that has grown into one of the world's largest business software providers, reporting more than 110,000 employees across over 157 countries and non-IFRS revenue of 36.8 billion euros for fiscal year 2025. The company's core business is enterprise resource planning and related cloud applications for finance, procurement, human resources, supply chain, and customer engagement, delivered to customers worldwide, including through SAP Americas, which the company describes as covering more than 70 locations across North and South America.

A facility carrying an internal "COS" code naming convention in a business is typically part of a company's own operational real estate rather than a customer facing product, and Colorado Springs has for decades been home to a concentration of technology, aerospace, and telecommunications operations, including large corporate office and data campuses along the InterQuest corridor near Interstate 25, making it a plausible location for a company operated facility supporting SAP's internal computing, network, or business continuity needs in the western United States.

SAP's public corporate materials describe the company's global footprint in broad terms, such as its Labs network and Experience Centers, but do not name or describe a Colorado Springs facility, its square footage, its power capacity, or its function in any public document identified during research for this entry. That absence is itself informative: unlike Segra or Serverfarm, SAP is not in the business of marketing colocation space, so facilities like this one exist to serve the company's own operations rather than to attract tenants, and enterprise software companies of SAP's size routinely operate regional data or office facilities without public disclosure of technical specifications, treating that information as internal infrastructure detail rather than a matter of public record. No El Paso County property, permit, or zoning record specific to this address was identified during research for this entry. Absent such a record becoming available, what can be documented here is limited to the facility's general location, its operator's scale and business, and the broader technology corridor context of the InterQuest Ridge area in which it sits.

reading:
SAP SE is a German enterprise software company headquartered in Walldorf, primarily listed in Frankfurt and also listed in New York under the ticker SAP, filing with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission as a foreign private issuer on Form 20-F. It sells enterprise resource planning and related cloud applications rather than data centre space, and it appears in this registry for the same reason any large software company does, because the cloud half of its business runs on computing sites the company builds and owns for itself. The registry holds one United States row for SAP, carrying the internal site code COS02, in the InterQuest Ridge area on the north side of Colorado Springs, in El Paso County, Colorado.

What is publicly established sits mostly on the developer's side of the transaction rather than SAP's. T5 Data Centers assembled a 64 acre campus in Colorado Springs restricted by covenant to data centre use, marketed as T5 at Colorado, with dual independent utility feeds described as expandable to 100 megawatts of critical electrical capacity across the whole campus, an electricity rate quoted at 4.44 cents per kilowatt hour, and outside air conditions permitting free cooling more than 97 percent of the year. The first phase was completed in the first quarter of 2014, with a projected total investment of about 800 million dollars and 400 to 600 direct jobs. In June 2016 T5 announced that the campus had signed its first tenant, described only as a global enterprise software company and one of the top ten technology companies, which had bought 8.5 acres to build two synchronous data centres. Trade reporting identified the buyer as SAP America and put the transaction at 9 acres for 3 million dollars. The acreage figures differ by half an acre between the two accounts and both are recorded here rather than reconciled.

That land purchase matters for how this row should be read. SAP did not lease white space from a wholesale provider in the ordinary colocation sense. It bought a parcel inside a third party campus and built on it, which places the relationship closer to owner occupation with shared campus utility infrastructure than to tenancy. The 100 megawatt figure is campus wide utility capacity that T5 marketed as expandable across all 64 acres, and it is not SAP's power draw, service size or IT load. No IT load figure, utility service size, standby generator rating or building square footage has been published for COS02 by SAP, by T5 or in any filing. SAP's own corporate publications describe its global footprint in general terms and name no Colorado Springs site.

The registry's stored street value for this row is a reverse geocode to Windswept View on InterQuest Ridge, which is a nearest street answer rather than a verified postal address. The stored coordinates sit roughly a fifth of a mile from the separately recorded Walmart Colorado data centre, reflecting the concentration of large computing buildings along the Federal Drive and InterQuest corridor rather than any shared ownership between the two.
